units.text: Article 14
units.label: Art. 14

units.text: 1. The Russian Federation is a secular State. No religion may be established as a state or mandatory religion.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 14

units.text: 2. Religious associations are separate from the State and equal before the law.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 14

units.text: Article 15
units.label: Art. 15

units.text: 1. The Constitution of the Russian Federation has supreme legal force and direct effect and applies throughout the territory of the Russian Federation. Laws and other legal acts adopted in the Russian Federation must not contradict the Constitution of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 15

units.text: 2. Bodies of state authority, local self-government bodies, officials, citizens and their associations are obliged to observe the Constitution of the Russian Federation and the laws.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 15

units.text: 3. Laws are subject to official publication. Unpublished laws do not apply. Any normative legal acts affecting human and civil rights, freedoms and duties may not be applied unless officially published for general information.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 15

units.text: 4. Universally recognized principles and rules of international law and the international treaties of the Russian Federation form an integral part of its legal system. If an international treaty of the Russian Federation establishes rules different from those provided for by law, the rules of the international treaty apply.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 15

units.text: Article 16
units.label: Art. 16

units.text: 1. The provisions of this chapter of the Constitution constitute the foundations of the constitutional order of the Russian Federation and may be changed only in the manner established by this Constitution.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 16

units.text: 2. No other provisions of this Constitution may contradict the foundations of the constitutional order of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 16

units.locator: CHAPTER 2. HUMAN AND CIVIL RIGHTS AND FREEDOMS
units.text: CHAPTER 2. HUMAN AND CIVIL RIGHTS AND FREEDOMS
units.label: CHAPTER 2. HUMAN AND CIVIL RIGHTS AND FREEDOMS

units.text: Article 17
units.label: Art. 17

units.text: 1. In the Russian Federation, human and civil rights and freedoms are recognized and guaranteed according to universally recognized principles and rules of international law and in accordance with this Constitution.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 17

units.text: 2. Fundamental human rights and freedoms are inalienable and belong to everyone from birth.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 17

units.text: 3. The exercise of human and civil rights and freedoms must not violate the rights and freedoms of others.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 17

units.text: Article 18
units.label: Art. 18

units.text: Human and civil rights and freedoms have direct effect. They determine the meaning, content and application of laws, the activity of the legislative and executive authorities and local self-government, and are secured by the administration of justice.
units.label: Art. 18 · text

units.text: Article 19
units.label: Art. 19

units.text: 1. Everyone is equal before the law and the courts.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 19

units.text: 2. The State guarantees equality of human and civil rights and freedoms regardless of sex, race, ethnicity, language, origin, property or official status, place of residence, attitude to religion, beliefs, membership of public associations or other circumstances. All forms of restrictions on citizens' rights on grounds of social, racial, ethnic, linguistic or religious affiliation are prohibited.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 19

units.text: 3. Men and women have equal rights and freedoms and equal opportunities to exercise them.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 19

units.text: Article 20
units.label: Art. 20

units.text: 1. Everyone has the right to life.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 20

units.text: 2. Until its abolition, the death penalty may be established by federal law as an exceptional punishment for particularly serious crimes against life, provided that the accused is granted the right to have their case heard by a court sitting with a jury.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 20

units.text: Article 21
units.label: Art. 21

units.text: 1. The dignity of the individual is protected by the State. Nothing may serve as grounds for diminishing it.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 21

units.text: 2. No one shall be subjected to torture, violence or other cruel or degrading treatment or punishment. No one may be subjected to medical, scientific or other experiments without voluntary consent.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 21

units.text: Article 22
units.label: Art. 22

units.text: 1. Everyone has the right to liberty and personal inviolability.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 22

units.text: 2. Arrest, remand in custody and continued detention are permitted only by a court decision. Before a court decision, a person may not be detained for more than 48 hours.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 22

units.text: Article 23
units.label: Art. 23

units.text: 1. Everyone has the right to the inviolability of private life, personal and family privacy, and protection of their honour and good name.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 23

units.text: 2. Everyone has the right to privacy of correspondence, telephone conversations, postal, telegraphic and other communications. This right may be restricted only on the basis of a court decision.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 23

units.text: Article 24
units.label: Art. 24

units.text: 1. Collecting, storing, using and disseminating information about a person's private life without their consent is not permitted.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 24

units.text: 2. Bodies of state authority and local self-government bodies and their officials are obliged to ensure that everyone can inspect documents and materials directly affecting their rights and freedoms, unless otherwise provided by law.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 24

units.text: Article 25
units.label: Art. 25

units.text: The home is inviolable. No one may enter a home against the will of those living there except in cases established by federal law or on the basis of a court decision.
units.label: Art. 25 · text

units.text: Article 26
units.label: Art. 26

units.text: 1. Everyone is entitled to determine and indicate their ethnic affiliation. No one may be compelled to determine or indicate their ethnic affiliation.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 26

units.text: 2. Everyone has the right to use their native language and freely to choose the language of communication, upbringing, education and creative activity.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 26

units.text: Article 27
units.label: Art. 27

units.text: 1. Everyone lawfully present in the territory of the Russian Federation has the right to move freely and to choose their place of stay and residence.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 27

units.text: 2. Everyone may freely leave the Russian Federation. A citizen of the Russian Federation has the right to return to the Russian Federation without hindrance.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 27

units.text: Article 28
units.label: Art. 28

units.text: Everyone is guaranteed freedom of conscience and freedom of religion, including the right to profess any religion individually or jointly with others or to profess none, freely to choose, hold and disseminate religious and other beliefs and to act in accordance with them.
units.label: Art. 28 · text

units.text: Article 29
units.label: Art. 29

units.text: 1. Everyone is guaranteed freedom of thought and speech.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 29

units.text: 2. Propaganda or agitation inciting social, racial, ethnic or religious hatred and enmity is not permitted. Propaganda of social, racial, ethnic, religious or linguistic supremacy is prohibited.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 29

units.text: 3. No one may be compelled to express their opinions and beliefs or to renounce them.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 29

units.text: 4. Everyone has the right freely to seek, receive, transmit, produce and disseminate information by any lawful means. The list of information constituting state secrets is determined by federal law.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 29

units.text: 5. Freedom of the mass media is guaranteed. Censorship is prohibited.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 29

units.text: Article 30
units.label: Art. 30

units.text: 1. Everyone has the right of association, including the right to establish trade unions to protect their interests. Freedom of activity of public associations is guaranteed.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 30

units.text: 2. No one may be compelled to join or remain in any association.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 30

units.text: Article 31
units.label: Art. 31

units.text: Citizens of the Russian Federation have the right to assemble peacefully and without weapons and to hold meetings, rallies, demonstrations, marches and pickets.
units.label: Art. 31 · text

units.text: Article 32
units.label: Art. 32

units.text: 1. Citizens of the Russian Federation have the right to participate in administering state affairs both directly and through their representatives.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 32

units.text: 2. Citizens of the Russian Federation have the right to elect and be elected to bodies of state authority and local self-government bodies, and to participate in referendums.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 32

units.text: 3. Citizens declared legally incapable by a court, and those held in places of deprivation of liberty under a court sentence, have no right to elect or be elected.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 32

units.text: 4. Citizens of the Russian Federation have equal access to state service.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 32

units.text: 5. Citizens of the Russian Federation have the right to participate in the administration of justice.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 32
